output.problem: Operators need a concise example explaining when a confirmed recoverable technical failure can receive a linked retry, without confusing elapsed time or a failed job with retry authority. Refine that documentation task for issue #359 while retaining the existing minimum delay, retry budget and fail-closed checks.
affectedUsers: Repository owners deciding whether to request further work after a technical failure.
Workflow maintainers inspecting linked retry evidence and retiring the disposable acceptance fixture.
output.desiredOutcome: A short operator-facing example, suitable for the package's existing recovery guidance, explains a minimum 30-minute wait after the preceding failed execution ends and no more than two linked retries per original request, conditional on all existing safety checks.

Use src/packages/sdlc/handoffs.md#recovery and src/packages/sdlc/github-actions.md#worker-maintenance as the existing policy references.
Distinguish a hypothetical operator example from verified native execution evidence for the disposable #359 fixture.
constraints: Only refinement is authorized. request.autoImplement is false; no automatic implementation is requested.

Do not change the minimum delay, original-request retry budget, authorization, cancellation, reservation, human-decision or uncertain-effect gates.
A short failure is not proof of a provider outage, and waiting alone does not make a failure retryable.

Any later fixture operation must remain restricted to issue #359, retain the original failure and immutable request chain, preserve prior repository variable values and retire the temporary activation afterward.

illustrativeContent.kind: Refinement illustration only; not a published document, formal proposal or native execution receipt.
illustrativeContent.text: Suppose a confirmed recoverable technical failure ends at 10:00. If all existing recovery checks still pass, its first linked retry cannot start before 10:30; any second linked retry must likewise wait at least 30 minutes after the preceding failed execution ends. The original request permits at most two linked retries, and each retry retains its own immutable request linked to the original failure. Waiting does not authorize retry: cancellation, changed authority, human holds, missing evidence and uncertain publication still stop recovery. Exhaustion requires a new owner decision.
